{{short description|American mathematician}}
'''Tristan Needham''' is a British [[mathematician]] and professor of mathematics at the [[University of San Francisco]], best known to the public for his books ''Visual Complex Analysis'', and ''Visual Differential Geometry and Forms''.

==Education, career and publications==

Tristan is the son of [[social anthropologist]] [[Rodney Needham]] of [[Oxford, England]]. He attended the [[Dragon School]]. Later Needham attended the [[University of Oxford]] and studied [[physics]] at [[Merton College]], and then transferred to the [[Mathematical Institute, University of Oxford|Mathematical Institute]] where he studied under [[Roger Penrose]]. He obtained his D.Phil. in 1987 and in 1989 took up his post at University of San Francisco.<ref>[http://www.usfca.edu/facultydetails.aspx?id=4294969533 Faculty profile] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120607222327/http://www.usfca.edu/facultydetails.aspx?id=4294969533 |date=2012-06-07 }} from [[University of San Francisco]]</ref><ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20150102045544/https://www.usfca.edu/about/history/changing-course/ University of San Francisco website – History of the Sciences: Changing Course.]</ref>

In 1993 he published ''A Visual Explanation of [[Jensen's inequality]]''.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Needham |first=Tristan |date=1993 |title=A Visual Explanation of Jensen's Inequality |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/2324783 |journal=The American Mathematical Monthly |volume=100 |issue=8 |pages=768–771 |doi=10.2307/2324783|jstor=2324783 }}</ref> The following year he published ''The Geometry of Harmonic Functions'', which won the [[Carl B. Allendoerfer Award]] for 1995.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Needham |first=Tristan |date=1994 |title=The Geometry of Harmonic Functions |url=https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/0025570X.1994.11996195 |journal=Mathematics Magazine |language=en |volume=67 |issue=2 |pages=92–108 |doi=10.1080/0025570X.1994.11996195 |issn=0025-570X|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>[http://www.maa.org/allendoerfer-award Allendoerfer Award] from [[Mathematics Association of America]]</ref>

Needham wrote the book ''Visual Complex Analysis'', which has received positive reviews.<ref>
Frank A. Farris (1998) ''American Mathematical Monthly'', 105(6):570: "''Visual Complex Analysis'' will show you the field of complex analysis in a way you almost certainly have not seen it before".</ref> Though it is described as a "radical first course in [[complex analysis]] aimed at undergraduates", writing in ''[[Mathematical Reviews]]'' D.H. Armitage said that "the book will be appreciated most by those who already know some complex analysis."<ref>[http://www.ams.org/mathscinet/pdf/1446490.pdf Review of ''Visual Complex Analysis''] from [[Mathematical Reviews]]</ref> In fact [[Douglas Hofstadter]] wrote "Needham's work of art with its hundreds and hundreds of beautiful figures á la Latta, brings complex analysis alive in an unprecedented manner".<ref>Preface page xvi of Chris Pritchard (2003) ''Changing Shape of Geometry'', [[Cambridge University Press]] {{ISBN|0521531624}}</ref> Hofstadter had studied complex analysis at Stanford with [[Gordon Latta]], and he recalled "Latta's amazingly precise and elegant blackboard diagrams". In 2001 a German language version, translated by Norbert Herrmann and Ina Paschen, was published by R. Oldenbourg Verlag, Munich.

In 2021, Needham published ''Visual Differential Geometry and Forms: A Mathematical Drama in Five Acts ([[Princeton University Press]])''<ref>{{Cite book|last=Needham|first=Tristan|url=https://press.princeton.edu/books/hardcover/9780691203690/visual-differential-geometry-and-forms|title=Visual Differential Geometry and Forms: A Mathematical Drama in Five Acts|publisher=Princeton University Press|year=2021|isbn=9780691203690 }}</ref>''.'' (The original title was ''Visual Differential Geometry''.) Much of this material was already developed in the writing of ''Visual Complex Analysis''.
